anomalies.observed: The anode of the second LED in dual LED D30 (A2, pin 4) sits on ESTOP_OUT. Its cathode K2 (pin 2) reaches the same ESTOP_OUT net through R60. The LED therefore has both terminals on one net and cannot be forward-biased. The first channel is wired correctly: A1 (pin 3) is on /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV and K1 goes through R59 to GND.
anomalies.expected: By the pattern of the first channel, A2 should be on the LED power rail /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, with K2 switched through R60 to ESTOP_OUT. That gives a working e-stop indicator that lights when ESTOP_OUT is pulled low.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop indicator channel D30 (LED2) never lights. Operators lose the visual e-stop status indication, and the ESTOP_OUT net is loaded by an LED anode it should not see.

anomalies.observed: Red LED D2 has its anode on the open-drain output U27.4 (Y) and its cathode pulled to GND through R31 (200R). SN74LVC1G07 is open-drain, and no pull-up exists on Net-(D2-A), so the anode is never driven high and D2 cannot light. The other status LEDs (D12, D17) use the reverse arrangement: anode to +3V3 through a resistor, cathode on the open-drain output.
anomalies.expected: A status LED driven from an open-drain buffer should have its anode pulled up to the supply through a resistor and its cathode on the buffer output, as on D12 and D17.

evidence.quote: /{slash}LED_EN : R33.2(2,passive) SW7.5(passive) U1.1(/OE,input) U18.1(/OE,input) U19.1(/OE,input) U27.1(/OE,input) U34.1(/OE,input)

anomalies.impact: The red status LED D2 is dark at all times, so the indicator that should show its state gives no feedback.

anomalies.observed: The LTC4412 ideal-diode PFET Q1 has its source (pin 2) on +5V, the output side. Its drain (pin 3) is on USBC_VBUS_IN, the input side. The LTC4412 VIN pin is on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE is on +5V, so the FET is wired with source and drain reversed for an ideal-diode OR where the input should feed the source.
anomalies.expected: For an LTC4412 ideal-diode path, the P-channel FET source should be on the input supply (VIN, USBC_VBUS_IN), with the drain on the load (+5V). The body diode then conducts input to output as the reverse-current protection intends.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) J3.A9(VBUS,passive) J3.B4(VBUS,passive) J3.B9(VBUS,passive) Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: With the FET source and drain swapped relative to the controller's intended topology, the body diode blocks the USB-to-+5V path when the FET is off, so reverse-current and power-path behaviour may not match the design.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows the e-stop LED channel D30 with its anode bridged onto ESTOP_OUT, leaving that LED permanently unlit. Secondary concerns are the red LED D2, which has no pull-up for its open-drain drive, and the reversed source/drain on the LTC4412 PFET Q1; these are less certain.
